boards.name: ICSE
boards.description: ICSE (Class 10) and ISC (Class 12) are conducted by the Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE). Classes 6 to 9 and 11 are school-examined on the CISCE syllabus.

history-civics.overview: ICSE History & Civics is Paper 1 of History, Civics and Geography (H.C.G., subject code 50). In Class X it is one 2-hour paper of 80 marks plus 20 marks of internal assessment (a project marked by internal and external examiners). Section A (Civics) covers the Union Legislature, the Union Executive and the Judiciary. Section B (History) covers the Indian National Movement (1857–1917), the Mass Phase of the National Movement (1915–1947) and the Contemporary World. The syllabus lists topics with lettered sub-topics, not chapters, so the sub-topics are used here as chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ICSE Examination Year 2027 syllabus: History, Civics and Geography (50), Paper 1 History & Civics, Class X

geography.overview: ICSE Geography is Paper 2 of History, Civics and Geography (H.C.G., subject code 50). In Class X it is one 2-hour paper of 80 marks plus 20 marks of internal assessment (project work). Part I (Map Work) covers interpretation of topographical maps and the map of India. Part II (Geography of India) covers climate, soil, natural vegetation, water, minerals and energy, agriculture, manufacturing industries, transport and waste management.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ICSE Examination Year 2027 syllabus: History, Civics and Geography (50), Paper 2 Geography, Class X

chapters.name: Interpretation of Topographical Maps

chapters.summary: Part II: Geography of India, Topic 6. Sources, conservation, rainwater harvesting and methods of irrigation.

chapters.name: Waste Management
chapters.summary: Part II: Geography of India, Topic 11. Impact of waste accumulation, safe disposal methods, and reduce, reuse and recycle.

physics.overview: ISC Class XII Physics has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper (Paper I) and a 30-mark Paper II made up of practical (15), project work (10) and practical file (5). The theory is organised into nine units from Electrostatics to Electronic Devices. The units' numbered sub-units match the rationalised NCERT chapter titles and are used here as chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ISC Examination Year 2027 syllabus: Physics, Class XII

chapters.name: Electric Charges and Fields
chapters.summary: Unit 1: Electrostatics (i). Coulomb's law, electric field and dipole, lines of force, and Gauss's theorem.

chapters.name: Electrostatic Potential, Potential Energy and Capacitance
chapters.summary: Unit 1: Electrostatics (ii). Potential and potential energy, capacitors and dielectrics.

chapters.name: Current Electricity
chapters.summary: Unit 2: Current Electricity. Drift velocity and mobility, Ohm's law, emf, Kirchhoff's laws, and electrical energy and billing.

chapters.name: Moving Charges and Magnetism
chapters.summary: Unit 3: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism (i). Oersted's experiment, the Biot-Savart law, Ampere's law, and forces on charges and conductors.

chapters.name: Magnetism and Matter
chapters.summary: Unit 3: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism (ii). The current loop as a magnetic dipole, and magnetic properties of materials.

chapters.name: Electromagnetic Induction
chapters.summary: Unit 4: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents (i).

chapters.name: Alternating Current
chapters.summary: Unit 4: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents (ii). RMS values, reactance, LCR circuits (phasors) and resonance.

chapters.name: Electromagnetic Waves
chapters.summary: Unit 5: Electromagnetic Waves. Displacement current, properties of EM waves, and the electromagnetic spectrum.

chapters.name: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments
chapters.summary: Unit 6: Optics (i). Reflection, refraction, prisms, lenses and optical instruments.

chapters.name: Wave Optics
chapters.summary: Unit 6: Optics (ii). Wavefronts, Huygens' principle, interference (Young's double slit) and diffraction.

chapters.name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
chapters.summary: Unit 7: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter. The photoelectric effect, Einstein's equation, and de Broglie waves (Davisson-Germer, qualitative).

chapters.name: Atoms
chapters.summary: Unit 8: Atoms and Nuclei (i). Rutherford's model, Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom, and spectral series.

chapters.name: Nuclei
chapters.summary: Unit 8: Atoms and Nuclei (ii). Composition and size of the nucleus, mass-energy relation, binding energy, fission and fusion.

chapters.name: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
chapters.summary: Unit 9: Electronic Devices (i) and (ii). Energy bands, p-n junction, diode as a rectifier, LED, photodiode, solar cell and the Zener diode as a voltage regulator.

chemistry.overview: ISC Class XII Chemistry has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper (Paper I) and a 30-mark Paper II made up of practical (15), project work (10) and practical file (5). The theory has 10 units weighted by branch: Physical Chemistry (units 1–3) 25 marks, Inorganic Chemistry (units 4–5) 14 marks and Organic Chemistry (units 6–10) 31 marks.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ISC Examination Year 2027 syllabus: Chemistry, Class XII

chapters.name: Biomolecules
chapters.summary: Organic Chemistry, Unit 10. Carbohydrates, proteins and nucleic acids (DNA and RNA).

biology.overview: ISC Class XII Biology has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper (Paper I) and a 30-mark Paper II made up of practical (15), project work (10) and practical file (5). The theory has five units: Reproduction (16 marks), Genetics and Evolution (15), Biology and Human Welfare (14), Biotechnology and its Applications (10), and Ecology and Environment (15). Their numbered sub-units are used here as chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ISC Examination Year 2027 syllabus: Biology, Class XII

mathematics.overview: ISC Class XII Mathematics (860) has a 3-hour, 80-mark theory paper (Paper I) and a 20-mark project (Paper II). The ISC 2027 syllabus is NOT divided into Sections A/B/C. It lists seven units: Relations and Functions (10 marks), Algebra (10), Calculus (35), Vector Algebra (5), Three-Dimensional Geometry (6), Linear Programming (5) and Probability (9). In the ISC 2026 syllabus, Section A (65 marks) was compulsory and candidates chose Section B (Vectors, 3-D Geometry, Applications of Integrals) or Section C (Application of Calculus, Linear Regression, Linear Programming) for 15 marks. The 2027 syllabus drops Application of Calculus (commerce) and Linear Regression, and all units are compulsory.

syllabusSource.title: CISCE, ISC Examination Year 2027 syllabus: Mathematics (860), Class XII

chapters.name: Probability
chapters.summary: Unit 7: Probability. Conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, random variables and their probability distributions and mean.

boards.name: CBSE
boards.description: CBSE conducts the Class 10 (Secondary School) and Class 12 (Senior School Certificate) board examinations and publishes its board question papers and marking schemes on cbse.gov.in. Classes 6 to 9 and 11 are school-examined on the NCERT-based syllabus.

science.overview: CBSE Class 10 Science (subject code 086) follows the NCERT textbook and covers chemistry (reactions, acids and bases, metals, carbon compounds), biology (life processes, control and coordination, reproduction, heredity, environment) and physics (light, the human eye, electricity and magnetism). The board paper is 80 marks in 3 hours, with 20 marks of internal assessment.
studyTips: Work through the official CBSE question papers and marking schemes for recent years: the marking scheme shows the value points examiners look for.
Practise balanced chemical equations and ray diagrams until you can draw them without looking.
For case-based questions, read the passage first and underline the data each sub-part refers to.
Revise definitions and laws word for word; short answers are marked against specific value points.

chapters.name: Chemical Reactions and Equations
chapters.summary: Writing and balancing chemical equations, and the main types of reactions: combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement and redox, with everyday effects such as corrosion and rancidity.

chapters.name: Acids, Bases and Salts
chapters.summary: Properties and reactions of acids and bases, indicators and the pH scale, and the preparation and uses of common salts such as baking soda, washing soda and bleaching powder.

chapters.name: Metals and Non-metals
chapters.summary: Physical and chemical properties of metals and non-metals, the reactivity series, ionic compounds, extraction of metals and prevention of corrosion.

chapters.name: Carbon and its Compounds
chapters.summary: Covalent bonding in carbon, versatile nature of carbon, homologous series, functional groups and nomenclature, and the chemical properties of carbon compounds including ethanol and ethanoic acid, soaps and detergents.

chapters.name: Life Processes
chapters.summary: Nutrition, respiration, transportation and excretion in plants and humans.

chapters.name: Control and Coordination
chapters.summary: The nervous system, reflex actions and the human brain, coordination in plants through plant hormones, and hormones in animals.

chapters.name: How do Organisms Reproduce?
chapters.summary: Modes of asexual reproduction, sexual reproduction in flowering plants and humans, and reproductive health.

chapters.name: Heredity
chapters.summary: Accumulation of variation, Mendel's experiments and rules of inheritance, and sex determination.

chapters.name: Light – Reflection and Refraction
chapters.summary: Reflection by spherical mirrors, refraction through glass slabs and spherical lenses, the mirror and lens formulae, magnification and power of a lens.

chapters.name: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
chapters.summary: Structure and defects of the human eye and their correction, refraction through a prism, dispersion, atmospheric refraction and scattering of light.
topics: The human eye and its defects

chapters.name: Electricity
chapters.summary: Electric current and potential difference, Ohm's law, resistance and resistivity, resistors in series and parallel, heating effect of current and electric power.

chapters.name: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
chapters.summary: Magnetic field and field lines, the field due to a current-carrying conductor, force on a conductor in a magnetic field, and domestic electric circuits.
topics: Field due to a current-carrying conductor

chapters.name: Our Environment
chapters.summary: Ecosystems and their components, food chains and webs, trophic levels, and how human activities affect the environment, including ozone depletion and waste management.

mathematics.overview: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics is examined at two levels, Standard (041) and Basic (241), on the same NCERT syllabus: number systems, algebra, coordinate geometry, geometry, trigonometry, mensuration, statistics and probability. The board paper is 80 marks in 3 hours, with 20 marks of internal assessment.
studyTips: Solve the official CBSE question papers for recent years under timed conditions, then compare your working with the marking scheme.
Write every step: the marking scheme awards marks for method as well as the final answer.
Keep a formula sheet for mensuration and trigonometry and revise it daily in the last month.
Case-based questions often combine two chapters; identify which formula each sub-part needs before calculating.

chapters.name: Real Numbers
chapters.summary: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, HCF and LCM, and proofs of irrationality.

chapters.name: Polynomials
chapters.summary: Zeroes of a polynomial and the relationship between zeroes and coefficients of quadratic polynomials.

chapters.name: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
chapters.summary: Graphical and algebraic methods (substitution and elimination) for solving a pair of linear equations, and consistency of the system.

chapters.name: Quadratic Equations
chapters.summary: Solving quadratic equations by factorisation and the quadratic formula, and the nature of roots.

chapters.name: Arithmetic Progressions
chapters.summary: The nth term and the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic progression, with applications.

chapters.name: Triangles
chapters.summary: Similarity of triangles, the Basic Proportionality Theorem and criteria for similarity.

chapters.name: Coordinate Geometry
chapters.summary: The distance formula and the section formula.

chapters.name: Introduction to Trigonometry
chapters.summary: Trigonometric ratios, ratios of specific angles, and trigonometric identities.

chapters.name: Some Applications of Trigonometry
chapters.summary: Heights and distances using angles of elevation and depression.

chapters.name: Circles
chapters.summary: Tangents to a circle and the number and properties of tangents from an external point.

chapters.name: Areas Related to Circles
chapters.summary: Areas of sectors and segments of a circle.

chapters.name: Surface Areas and Volumes
chapters.summary: Surface areas and volumes of combinations of solids.

chapters.name: Statistics
chapters.summary: Mean, median and mode of grouped data.
topics: Mode and median of grouped data

chapters.name: Probability
chapters.summary: Theoretical probability of simple events.

social-science.overview: CBSE Class 10 Social Science (code 087) is examined through an 80-mark board paper made up of four 20-mark parts: History (India and the Contemporary World – II), Geography (Contemporary India – II), Political Science (Democratic Politics – II) and Economics (Understanding Economic Development). A further 20 marks are internally assessed through periodic tests, an interdisciplinary project, a portfolio and subject enrichment activities. Some chapters or subtopics are assessed only internally or only through map work, as noted chapter by chapter.

syllabusSource.title: CBSE Secondary Curriculum 2025-26: Social Science (Code 087), Class X course structure and internal assessment

physics.overview: CBSE Class 12 Physics (code 042) has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper across 9 units and 14 NCERT chapters, plus 30 marks of practicals. The units run from Electrostatics to Electronic Devices and follow the rationalised NCERT Class XII Physics Parts I and II.

syllabusSource.title: CBSE Senior Secondary Curriculum 2025-26: Physics (Code 042), Class XII

chapters.name: Electric Charges and Fields
chapters.summary: Unit I: Electrostatics. Coulomb's law, electric field and dipoles, electric flux and Gauss's theorem.

chapters.name: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance
chapters.summary: Unit I: Electrostatics. Potential, equipotential surfaces, potential energy, dielectrics and capacitors.

chapters.name: Current Electricity
chapters.summary: Unit II: Current Electricity. Drift velocity, Ohm's law, resistivity, emf and internal resistance, Kirchhoff's rules and the Wheatstone bridge.

chapters.name: Magnetism and Matter

chapters.name: Electromagnetic Induction

chapters.name: Alternating Current
chapters.summary: Unit IV: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents. RMS values, reactance and impedance, LCR circuits, resonance, power factor, AC generator and transformer.

chapters.name: Electromagnetic Waves

chapters.name: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments

chapters.name: Wave Optics
chapters.summary: Unit VI: Optics. Huygens' principle, interference and Young's double slit, and single-slit diffraction.

chapters.name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
chapters.summary: Unit VII: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter. The photoelectric effect, Einstein's equation and de Broglie matter waves.

chapters.name: Atoms
chapters.summary: Unit VIII: Atoms and Nuclei. Alpha-particle scattering, Rutherford's model, and the Bohr model and line spectra of hydrogen.

chapters.name: Nuclei
chapters.summary: Unit VIII: Atoms and Nuclei. Nuclear composition and size, mass defect, binding energy, fission and fusion.

chapters.name: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
chapters.summary: Unit IX: Electronic Devices. Energy bands, intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors, the p-n junction, and the diode as a rectifier.

chemistry.overview: CBSE Class 12 Chemistry (code 043) has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper over 10 units, plus 30 marks of practicals. The syllabus covers physical chemistry (solutions, electrochemistry, kinetics), inorganic chemistry (d- and f-block elements, coordination compounds) and organic chemistry (haloalkanes to biomolecules). It is based on the NCERT Class XII Chemistry Parts I and II.

syllabusSource.title: CBSE Senior Secondary Curriculum 2025-26: Chemistry (Code 043), Class XII

chapters.name: Solutions
chapters.summary: Unit 1 (7 marks). Concentration, Raoult's law, colligative properties and the van't Hoff factor.

chapters.name: Electrochemistry
chapters.summary: Unit 2 (9 marks). EMF, the Nernst equation, conductance, Kohlrausch's law, batteries, fuel cells and corrosion.

chapters.name: Chemical Kinetics
chapters.summary: Unit 3 (7 marks). Rate laws, order and molecularity, integrated rate equations, half-life and the Arrhenius equation.

chapters.name: d- and f-Block Elements
chapters.summary: Unit 4 (7 marks). Trends in transition metals, K2Cr2O7 and KMnO4, lanthanides and actinides.

chapters.name: Coordination Compounds
chapters.summary: Unit 5 (7 marks). Ligands, IUPAC nomenclature, Werner's theory, VBT and CFT, and isomerism.

chapters.name: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
chapters.summary: Unit 6 (6 marks). The C–X bond, substitution mechanisms, and uses and environmental effects of polyhalogen compounds.

chapters.name: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
chapters.summary: Unit 7 (6 marks). Preparation, properties and uses of alcohols, phenols and ethers.

chapters.name: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
chapters.summary: Unit 8 (8 marks). The carbonyl group, nucleophilic addition, alpha-hydrogen reactivity, and carboxylic acids.

chapters.name: Amines
chapters.summary: Unit 9 (6 marks). Classification, preparation and properties of amines, and diazonium salts.

chapters.name: Biomolecules
chapters.summary: Unit 10 (7 marks). Carbohydrates, proteins, enzymes, vitamins and nucleic acids.

biology.overview: CBSE Class 12 Biology (code 044) has a 3-hour, 70-mark theory paper across five units (VI–X) and 13 chapters, plus 30 marks of practicals. The units are Reproduction (16 marks), Genetics and Evolution (20), Biology and Human Welfare (12), Biotechnology and its Applications (12), and Ecology and Environment (10).

syllabusSource.title: CBSE Senior Secondary Curriculum 2025-26: Biology (Code 044), Class XII

chapters.name: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
chapters.summary: Unit VI: Reproduction. Flower structure, gametophytes, pollination, double fertilisation, seed and fruit formation.

chapters.name: Human Reproduction
chapters.summary: Unit VI: Reproduction. Reproductive systems, gametogenesis, the menstrual cycle, fertilisation, implantation and pregnancy.

chapters.name: Reproductive Health
chapters.summary: Unit VI: Reproduction. STD prevention, contraception, MTP, amniocentesis, infertility and ART.

chapters.name: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
chapters.summary: Unit VII: Genetics and Evolution. Mendelian inheritance and deviations, sex determination, linkage, and genetic disorders.

chapters.name: Molecular Basis of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Unit VII: Genetics and Evolution. DNA structure and replication, the central dogma, the lac operon, genome projects and DNA fingerprinting.

chapters.name: Evolution
chapters.summary: Unit VII: Genetics and Evolution. The origin of life, evidences and mechanisms of evolution, Hardy-Weinberg principle and human evolution.

chapters.name: Human Health and Diseases
chapters.summary: Unit VIII: Biology and Human Welfare. Pathogens and diseases, immunology and vaccines, cancer, HIV/AIDS, and drug and alcohol abuse.

chapters.name: Microbes in Human Welfare
chapters.summary: Unit VIII: Biology and Human Welfare. Microbes in food, industry, sewage treatment, energy, biocontrol and biofertilisers.

chapters.name: Biotechnology - Principles and Processes
chapters.summary: Unit IX: Biotechnology and its Applications. Genetic engineering (recombinant DNA technology).

chapters.name: Biotechnology and its Applications
chapters.summary: Unit IX: Biotechnology and its Applications. Insulin and vaccine production, gene therapy, Bt crops, transgenic animals and biosafety.

chapters.name: Organisms and Populations
chapters.summary: Unit X: Ecology and Environment. Population interactions and population attributes.

chapters.name: Ecosystem
chapters.summary: Unit X: Ecology and Environment. Ecosystem components, productivity, decomposition, energy flow and ecological pyramids.

chapters.name: Biodiversity and its Conservation
chapters.summary: Unit X: Ecology and Environment. Patterns and loss of biodiversity, hotspots and in-situ/ex-situ conservation.

mathematics.overview: CBSE Class 12 Mathematics (code 041) has one 80-mark theory paper and 20 marks of internal assessment. The paper covers six units: Relations and Functions (8 marks), Algebra (10), Calculus (35), Vectors and Three-Dimensional Geometry (14), Linear Programming (5) and Probability (8). These units contain 13 NCERT chapters.

syllabusSource.title: CBSE Senior Secondary Curriculum 2025-26: Mathematics (Code 041), Class XII

chapters.name: Relations and Functions
chapters.summary: Unit I: Relations and Functions. Types of relations, equivalence relations, and one-one and onto functions.

chapters.name: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
chapters.summary: Unit I: Relations and Functions. Domain, range, principal value branches and graphs.

chapters.name: Matrices
chapters.summary: Unit II: Algebra. Types of matrices, matrix operations, transpose, symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices, and invertibility.

chapters.name: Determinants
chapters.summary: Unit II: Algebra. Determinants up to 3 × 3, minors and cofactors, adjoint and inverse, and solving linear systems.

chapters.name: Continuity and Differentiability
chapters.summary: Unit III: Calculus. The chain rule, implicit and parametric differentiation, logarithmic differentiation and second-order derivatives.

chapters.name: Applications of Derivatives
chapters.summary: Unit III: Calculus. Rate of change, increasing and decreasing functions, and maxima and minima.

chapters.name: Integrals
chapters.summary: Unit III: Calculus. Integration by substitution, partial fractions and parts, and definite integrals and their properties.

chapters.name: Application of the Integrals
chapters.summary: Unit III: Calculus. Area under simple curves (lines, circles, parabolas, ellipses in standard form).

chapters.name: Differential Equations
chapters.summary: Unit III: Calculus. Order and degree, separation of variables, and homogeneous and linear first-order equations.

chapters.name: Vectors
chapters.summary: Unit IV: Vectors and Three-Dimensional Geometry. Types of vectors, components, section formula, and dot and cross products.

chapters.name: Three-dimensional Geometry
chapters.summary: Unit IV: Vectors and Three-Dimensional Geometry. Direction cosines and ratios, equations of a line, skew lines and shortest distance.

chapters.name: Linear Programming
chapters.summary: Unit V: Linear Programming Problem. Graphical solution of two-variable problems with up to three non-trivial constraints.

chapters.name: Probability
chapters.summary: Unit VI: Probability. Conditional probability, the multiplication theorem, independent events, total probability and Bayes' theorem.
